name: parcad
description: Design parts for 3D printing and machining. ParCAD's CAD kernel builds each part from a short script, measures it and checks it before you export 3MF, STEP or STL.

interface.longDescription:
Describe a part. Get one that fits.

Ask ChatGPT for a bracket, a box with a hinged lid, a stand for your phone. ParCAD builds it on a real CAD kernel and checks it before you print: the size you asked for, the walls, whether the lid actually closes.

Download a 3MF for your slicer or a STEP for any CAD.

Free and open source. Sign in with Google or GitHub.
defaultPrompt: A wall bracket for a 25 mm pipe
A box for a deck of cards with a hinged lid
A stand for my phone at 60°

positive.description: Design a new part from a description, report the size ParCAD measured and show it in 3D.
positive.prompt: Using ParCAD, design a phone stand 70 mm wide that holds the phone leaning back at 65 degrees, with a lip at the front and a slot for the charging cable. Tell me its measured size and show it to me in 3D.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads ParCAD's language docs with read_docs, writes the stand as a script and builds it with evaluate_part, then saves it with save_project and opens it with open_project. ParCAD's 3D viewer shows the stand in the chat. The reply gives the size ParCAD measured (70 mm wide) and the outcome of its checks.

positive.description: Build a part and hand the user a printable 3MF file.
positive.prompt: Using ParCAD, make a 30 mm knurled knob with a 6 mm D-shaped shaft hole and give me a 3MF file I can print.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT builds the knob with evaluate_part and exports it with export_part. The reply links a .3mf download on mcp.parcad.dev that opens in any slicer, and gives the size ParCAD measured (30 mm across) and that the part is watertight.

positive.description: Open one of the example parts every account starts with and show it in 3D.
positive.prompt: Show me the spur gears from my ParCAD parts in 3D.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT opens spur-gears with open_project, after list_projects if it needs the path. ParCAD's 3D viewer appears in the chat with the pinion and the wheel meshed as two bodies; the user can turn it, see through it and hide either gear.

positive.description: Measure the clearance between two parts of a saved design on the exact solids.
positive.prompt: Using ParCAD, how much clearance is there between the two gears in my spur-gears part?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT builds spur-gears with evaluate_part and reads the measurement between its two bodies. The reply says the gears are clear of each other by 0.094 mm, as ParCAD measured it.

positive.description: Change a saved part and report what the change did to it.
positive.prompt: Using ParCAD, make the knurled knob in my parts 5 mm taller and tell me how its volume changed.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads knurled-knob with read_project and changes its height with edit_part, which builds the change before saving it. The reply gives the old and new height and the volume before and after, as ParCAD measured them.

negative.description: A general question about 3D-printing materials needs no part built.
negative.prompt: What's the difference between PLA and PETG filament for 3D printing?

negative.description: Shopping for a printer is not part design, so ParCAD is not called.
negative.prompt: Find me a good 3D printer under 300 dollars.

negative.description: A drawing or picture is not a part to model.
negative.prompt: Draw me a picture of a cat wearing a party hat.

publication.release_notes: First release for ChatGPT. Build parts with ParCAD's hosted CAD kernel, measure them (size, volume, wall thickness, fit), and export 3MF, STEP or STL by download link. Sign in with Google or GitHub; parts are kept in your own account.
